_doc: Fixed prompts for the painted card pass (owner_rulings.md ruling 30; art/tools/paint_card.py). A card's prompt = style + subject (per card, from the fighter's brief and palette) + light (filled from the card's plate: its sun side and glow colour) + eyes + rules + the imagegen SENSITIVITY line. Change a prompt only with a new version number: paint.json beside the cards records the version and the full text that made each card. Version 2 (cards third pass, verify 2): no added colour or part; the lens's blue ring is the figure's only blue; Long Evening keeps the render's warm festival grade (lead call: the render is canonical); the Shadeprint mask is ruling 2's amber lacquer with dark lidded eyes; Sukri's mask has no lines below the eyes. Version 3 (cards pass 4): paint only what the reference shows (a part named in the subject that is out of frame stays out: Sukri's portrait gained a crook and cup), no added light source, sun disc or lens, keep the reference's brightness (Highrim's portrait lifted the draft cell); a hands line (the card hands now have fingers, knuckles and a thumb: keep them); Sukri's cheeks and the band under the eyes are smooth unmarked wood on every Sukri card; the Shadeprint mask keeps its rendered amber (it turned saturated orange). cards_portrait: a portrait's subject when it differs (Sukri's staff, crook and cup are out of a portrait's frame; naming them made the painter add them, 3 of 3 variants in pass 4). v3 splash retry (same pass): Sukri's and Stillwater's splash subjects ask for a light paint on the face (the painter streaked the mask's grain in 6 of 6 splash variants; the portraits, painted lightly, held). Version 4 (cards ks1 fix): verify ks1 read saturated amber iris rings on Sukri's v2 portrait: the eyes line asks for irises as muted as the reference (and the pre-gate caps eye_ds at +15); Shadeprint's wraps are the game's muted slate with pale grey-lilac bands, not saturated violet (the card's plate cast is graded off them too). Version 5 (max2 card blockers): Burdam's and Dunsom's masks were rebuilt at the model (lidded carved eyes with irises and pupils, warm lacquer, Dunsom's cracks and slit recesses gone); their subjects and eye lines say so, and Dunsom's mask is one smooth surface with no crack or seam.
style: Repaint this exact image as one finished, hand-painted fantasy game key-art illustration: painterly brushwork with soft and lost edges over the figure and the landscape alike, painted form and light, a rich value structure. Keep the composition, the camera, the framing, the background layout and the character's pose, silhouette, proportions, costume parts and colours exactly as in the reference. Do not add or remove props, limbs or figures; do not move, turn or resize the character. Add no colour, ornament, band or part that is not in the reference. Paint only what is visible in the reference: anything described below that is out of frame stays out of frame. Add no object, light source, sun disc, lens or prop that the reference does not show. Keep the reference's overall brightness and the background's value; do not brighten the image.
light: Light: a low {glow} sun from the {side}, a warm rim light along the character's {side} edges, cooler shadow on the far side, a soft shadow cast from the feet onto the ground they stand on.
light_portrait: Light: a low {glow} sun from the {side}, a warm rim light along the character's {side} edges, cooler shadow on the far side.
eyes: Eyes: alive, with upper lids and dark pupils, looking out; never glowing, never solid colour, never empty or hollow, no bright or saturated ring round the iris; the irises exactly as muted and dark as in the reference, never more saturated or brighter.
rules: Painted form, not a 3D render; no outline halo. No text, no letters, no logo, no signature, no border, no frame.
